name: red brick, 1895 factory wall
facade: north-east face on rue de l'Inspecteur, the short side of the S4 outline

photo.title: File:Le Lowney - 005.jpg
photo.author: Jeangagnon
photo.saved_as: 3840 px wide copy from Wikimedia Commons, saved 2026-11-20

corners_note: top: the outer corners of the cornice; bottom: where the stone base meets the brick at each end of the face. Read by eye at full size; about 10 px either way.
width_source: S4 outline (OpenStreetMap way 54895065): the two short sides measure 17.89 m and 18.11 m
height_source: G1 height 22.25 m (2023 lidar, 90th percentile of the roof) less the stone base below the brick, 1.67 m, measured in the straightened photo (the base was first read at about 1.9 m)
checks: Storey in the straightened face: the left bay's window sills lie 3.50, 3.52 and 3.65 m apart (read by eye on face.jpg), against S4's measured storey of 3.55 m (all uses). Width came from the outline and height from the lidar, so the two scales agree.
Course height agrees across four separate patches of the face: 8.10 to 8.25 cm.
limits: At 1.25 pixels per cm a mortar joint (about 1 cm) is one pixel wide: the bond pattern and the brick length cannot be read from this photo.
The light lines are repointed joints, a later repair; most joints read darker than the brick.
Colour: one sunny afternoon in May 2016, camera white balance unknown.

base_color.how: the photo's colour; light changing over more than about 0.4 m divided out; the calmest 1.2 m window kept; tiled by a half-shift blend

height.how: estimated: brighter read as higher. Repointed light mortar reads as raised, the opposite of a recessed joint

normal.how: worked out from the estimated height with an assumed relief of 1 cm; OpenGL convention (green up)

roughness.how: one daylight photo shows no reflection to measure it

tile.chosen_by: fewest odd spots (repairs, stains) in a 10 cm search
